#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Reproduction script for the git version parsing issue.
This script reproduces the TypeError when git version contains letters.
"""

import re
from typing import Tuple

# Copy the exact regex from the source code
GIT_VERSION_REGEX = re.compile(
    r"^git version "  # Prefix.
    r"(\d+)"  # Major.
    r"\.(\d+)"  # Dot, minor.
    r"(?:\.(\d+))?"  # Optional dot, patch.
    r".*$"  # Suffix, including any pre- and post-release segments we don't care about.
)

def get_git_version(version_output: str) -> Tuple[int, ...]:
    """Simulate the problematic get_git_version method."""
    print(f"Parsing git version output: {version_output}")
    match = GIT_VERSION_REGEX.match(version_output)
    if not match:
        print("No match found")
        return ()
    
    print(f"Match groups: {match.groups()}")
    # This is the problematic line that causes TypeError
    try:

    15	## Overview
    16	
    17	The **nomenclature** package facilitates validation and processing of scenario data.
    18	It allows managing definitions of data structures for model comparison projects and
    19	scenario analysis studies using the data format developed by the
    20	[Integrated Assessment Modeling Consortium (IAMC)](https://www.iamconsortium.org).
    21	
    22	A data structure definition consists of one or several "codelists".
    23	A codelist is a list of allowed values (or "codes") for dimensions of IAMC-format data,
    24	typically *regions* and *variables*. Each code can have additional attributes:
    25	for example, a "variable" has to have an expected unit and usually has a description.
    26	Read the [SDMX Guidelines](https://sdmx.org/?page_id=4345) for more information on
    27	the concept of codelists.
    28	
    29	The **nomenclature** package supports three main use cases:
    30	
    31	- Management of codelists and mappings for model comparison projects
    32	- Validation of scenario data against the codelists of a specific project
    33	- Processing of scenario results, e.g. aggregation and renaming from "native regions" of
    34	  a model to "common regions" (i.e., regions that are used for scenario comparison in a project).
    35	
    36	The documentation is hosted on [Read the Docs](https://nomenclature-iamc.readthedocs.io/).
    37	
    38	## Integration with the pyam package
    39	
    40	<img src="https://github.com/IAMconsortium/pyam/blob/main/docs/logos/pyam-logo.png"
    41	width="133" height="100" align="right" alt="pyam logo" />
    42	
    43	The **nomenclature** package is designed to complement the Python package **pyam**,
    44	an open-source community toolbox for analysis & visualization of scenario data.
    45	The **pyam** package was developed to facilitate working with timeseries scenario data
    46	conforming to the format developed by the IAMC. It is used in ongoing assessments by
    47	the IPCC and in many model comparison projects at the global and national level,
    48	including several Horizon 2020 & Horizon Europe projects.
    49	
    50	The validation and processing features of the **nomenclature** package
